```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  warning = TRUE,
  cache = FALSE,
  fig.width = 7,
  fig.height = 4.8,
  fig.pos = "H"
)

library(readxl)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(emmeans)

# Output folder.
output_dir <- file.path("outputs", "biomass")
dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Confirmed mowing schedule relative to broccoli transplanting:
# T2: 1 week before, and 3 and 6 weeks after transplanting.
# T3: 1 week before, and 6 weeks after transplanting.
# T4: 1 week before transplanting only.
#
# Treatments remain categorical factors in the statistical model.

treatment_levels <- c("T4", "T3", "T2")

treatment_labels <- c(
  T4 = "T4\n-1 week",
  T3 = "T3\n-1 and +6 weeks",
  T2 = "T2\n-1, +3 and +6 weeks"
)

treatment_colours <- c(
  T4 = "#A56A46",
  T3 = "#4B8395",
  T2 = "#4A8862"
)

locations <- c("Broccoli", "Cover crop")

save_csv <- function(x, filename) {
  write.csv(
    x,
    file.path(output_dir, filename),
    row.names = FALSE,
    na = ""
  )
}

show_table <- function(x, caption, digits = 4) {
  cat("\n\n")

  print(knitr::kable(
    x,
    caption = caption,
    digits = digits,
    row.names = FALSE
  ))

  cat("\n\n")
}

make_anova_table <- function(model) {
  a <- as.data.frame(anova(model))

  data.frame(
    Term = rownames(a),
    a,
    row.names = NULL,
    check.names = FALSE
  )
}
```

## Research question

Does mowing treatment affect total recorded vegetation biomass
at broccoli harvest?

All three treatments were mown one week before broccoli transplanting.
Additional mowing followed the treatment-specific schedule:

- **T2:** mown at 3 and 6 weeks after transplanting,
  giving three mowing events in total.
- **T3:** mown at 6 weeks after transplanting,
  giving two mowing events in total.
- **T4:** no additional mowing after transplanting,
  giving one mowing event in total.

The analysis compares T2, T3, and T4 in four blocks.

All recorded species are included, including clovers and unidentified
taxa. The response is therefore total vegetation biomass.

## Sampling and statistical methods

The two sampling locations are analysed separately:

- **Broccoli:** quadrat area of 0.28 square metres; vegetation cut
  at ground level.
- **Cover crop:** quadrat area of 0.16 square metres; vegetation cut
  at 8 cm above ground.

Recorded masses are summed within each quadrat and divided by
quadrat area. The two quadrat densities are then averaged within
each plot and sampling location.

The plot is the experimental unit. Each sampling location contains
12 plot means: three treatments in four blocks.

For each location, the model is:

\[
\mathrm{Biomass}_{ij}
=
\mu + \mathrm{Treatment}_i + \mathrm{Block}_j
+ \varepsilon_{ij}.
\]

Treatment and block are fitted as categorical effects.
Tukey adjustment is applied to the three pairwise treatment
comparisons within each sampling location.

## Import and prepare the data

```{r import-and-clean, include=FALSE}
# GitHub source: 2-Data/Raw/
github_url <- paste0(
  "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/",
  "Pr1nc3sso/Xilei-Living-cover-crop/",
  "master/2-Data/Raw/",
  "Vegetation%20survey%20-%20broccoli%20harvest.xlsx"
)

options(timeout = max(120, getOption("timeout")))

excel_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".xlsx")

download.file(
  url = github_url,
  destfile = excel_file,
  mode = "wb",
  method = "libcurl",
  quiet = TRUE
)

# Read all populated rows in columns A:J.
# Do not restrict the import to a fixed final row.
raw <- read_excel(
  path = excel_file,
  sheet = "2026",
  range = cell_cols("A:J"),
  col_types = "text",
  trim_ws = FALSE
)

expected_headers <- c(
  "Biomass collection date",
  "Weeks after transplanting",
  "Block",
  "Treatment",
  "Quadrat",
  "Relative location to Broccoli: in row or in cover crop",
  "Species",
  "Biomass weight without bags, scale tared (gram)",
  "Quadrat size (m2)",
  "Weight date"
)

if (!identical(names(raw), expected_headers)) {
  stop("Excel headers have changed. Check the column mapping.")
}

# Preserve Excel row numbers before removing empty rows.
raw$excel_row <- seq_len(nrow(raw)) + 1L
raw <- raw[rowSums(!is.na(raw[1:10])) > 0, ]

# Compare only the ten original columns for exact duplicates.
# Records are not removed merely because their species labels match.
duplicate_flag <- duplicated(as.data.frame(raw[1:10]))

removed_duplicates <- raw[duplicate_flag, ]
clean <- raw[!duplicate_flag, ]

save_csv(
  removed_duplicates,
  "removed_exact_duplicates.csv"
)

names(clean)[1:10] <- c(
  "collection_date",
  "weeks_after_transplanting",
  "block",
  "treatment",
  "quadrat",
  "location",
  "species",
  "weight_g",
  "source_area_m2",
  "weighing_date"
)

clean <- clean %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      c(block, treatment, quadrat, weight_g, source_area_m2),
      as.numeric
    ),
    location = trimws(gsub("[[:space:]]+", " ", location)),
    species = toupper(trimws(species))
  )

# Validate identifiers and biomass weights.
numeric_fields <- c(
  "block",
  "treatment",
  "quadrat",
  "weight_g"
)

if (any(!is.finite(as.matrix(clean[numeric_fields])))) {
  stop("Missing or invalid identifiers or biomass weights.")
}

if (any(clean$weight_g < 0)) {
  stop("Negative biomass weights were found.")
}

if (
  any(!clean$block %in% 1:4) ||
  any(!clean$treatment %in% 1:4) ||
  any(!clean$quadrat %in% 1:4)
) {
  stop("Unexpected block, treatment, or quadrat identifiers.")
}

if (any(is.na(clean$species) | clean$species == "")) {
  stop("Some records have no species label.")
}

# Keep the three mowing treatments.
analysis_records <- clean %>%
  filter(treatment %in% 2:4)

if (any(!analysis_records$location %in% locations)) {
  stop("Unexpected or missing sampling-location labels.")
}

# Apply the confirmed areas while retaining the source values.
analysis_records <- analysis_records %>%
  mutate(
    area_m2 = if_else(
      location == "Broccoli",
      0.28,
      0.16
    )
  )

area_corrections <- analysis_records %>%
  filter(
    is.na(source_area_m2) |
      abs(source_area_m2 - area_m2) > 1e-10
  )

save_csv(
  area_corrections,
  "area_corrections.csv"
)

save_csv(
  analysis_records,
  "clean_T2_T4_records.csv"
)

# Avoid combining different collection dates within a quadrat.
date_check <- analysis_records %>%
  group_by(block, treatment, location, quadrat) %>%
  summarise(
    n_dates = n_distinct(
      collection_date,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

if (any(date_check$n_dates != 1)) {
  stop("Check missing or multiple collection dates within quadrats.")
}

# Sum all species and retained records within each quadrat.
quadrat_data <- analysis_records %>%
  group_by(block, treatment, location, quadrat) %>%
  summarise(
    total_weight_g = sum(weight_g),
    area_m2 = first(area_m2),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    biomass_g_m2 = total_weight_g / area_m2
  )

# Expected layout:
# 4 blocks x 3 treatments x 2 locations x 2 quadrats = 48 quadrats.
expected_quadrats <- expand_grid(
  block = 1:4,
  treatment = 2:4,
  location = locations,
  quadrat = 1:2
)

keys <- c(
  "block",
  "treatment",
  "location",
  "quadrat"
)

missing_quadrats <- anti_join(
  expected_quadrats,
  quadrat_data,
  by = keys
)

unexpected_quadrats <- anti_join(
  quadrat_data,
  expected_quadrats,
  by = keys
)

save_csv(
  missing_quadrats,
  "missing_quadrats.csv"
)

save_csv(
  unexpected_quadrats,
  "unexpected_quadrats.csv"
)

if (
  nrow(missing_quadrats) > 0 ||
  nrow(unexpected_quadrats) > 0
) {
  stop(
    "The quadrat layout differs from the complete design. ",
    "Check the exported missing/unexpected quadrat files. ",
    "Missing observations must not be replaced with zero."
  )
}

# Average the two quadrat densities within each plot and location.
plot_data <- quadrat_data %>%
  group_by(block, treatment, location) %>%
  summarise(
    n_quadrats = n(),
    biomass_g_m2 = mean(biomass_g_m2),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    block = factor(
      paste0("B", block),
      levels = paste0("B", 1:4)
    ),
    treatment = factor(
      paste0("T", treatment),
      levels = treatment_levels
    )
  )

if (any(plot_data$n_quadrats != 2)) {
  stop("Each plot and sampling location must contain two quadrats.")
}

save_csv(
  quadrat_data,
  "quadrat_biomass.csv"
)

save_csv(
  plot_data,
  "plot_biomass.csv"
)

# Save source information and the confirmed treatment descriptions.
writeLines(
  c(
    paste("Source:", github_url),
    paste(
      "Downloaded at UTC:",
      format(Sys.time(), tz = "UTC")
    ),
    paste(
      "File MD5:",
      unname(tools::md5sum(excel_file))
    ),
    "All T2-T4 treatments: mown 1 week before transplanting.",
    "T2: additional mowing at 3 and 6 weeks after transplanting.",
    "T3: additional mowing at 6 weeks after transplanting.",
    "T4: no additional mowing after transplanting."
  ),
  file.path(output_dir, "data_source.txt")
)
```

data_check <- data.frame(
  Item = c(
    "Original records",
    "Exact duplicates removed",
    "Records retained across all treatments",
    "Records included for T2-T4",
    "Area records corrected for T2-T4",
    "Quadrats included for T2-T4",

The confirmed sampling areas are used for conversion to biomass
per unit area. Any differences from the recorded Excel areas
are documented in the exported area-correction table.

## Fit the models and prepare figures

```{r models-and-figures, include=FALSE}
analyse_location <- function(location_name) {

  d <- plot_data %>%
    filter(location == location_name)

  # Verify one plot mean per block-treatment combination.
  if (
    nrow(d) != 12 ||
    !all(table(d$block, d$treatment) == 1)
  ) {
    stop("Expected one plot mean for each block-treatment combination.")
  }

  # Primary model: treatment and block as categorical effects.
  fit <- lm(
    biomass_g_m2 ~ treatment + block,
    data = d,
    na.action = na.fail
  )

  # Treatment and block are orthogonal in this balanced design.
  a <- anova(fit)
  anova_results <- make_anova_table(fit)

  # Calculate marginal means while the model data are available.
  emm <- emmeans::emmeans(
    fit,
    ~ treatment,
    weights = "equal"
  )

  # Individual 95% confidence intervals for adjusted means.
  mean_results <- as.data.frame(
    confint(
      emm,
      level = 0.95,
      adjust = "none"
    )
  )

  # Tukey-adjusted comparisons within this sampling location.
  tukey_results <- as.data.frame(
    summary(
      pairs(emm, adjust = "tukey"),
      infer = c(TRUE, TRUE),
      level = 0.95
    )
  )

  # Observed plot means and model-adjusted treatment means.
  figure <- ggplot() +
    geom_point(
      data = d,
      aes(
        x = treatment,
        y = biomass_g_m2,
        colour = treatment,
        shape = block
      ),
      position = position_jitter(
        width = 0.06,
        height = 0,
        seed = 42
      ),
      size = 2.8,
      alpha = 0.85
    ) +
    geom_errorbar(
      data = mean_results,
      aes(
        x = treatment,
        ymin = lower.CL,
        ymax = upper.CL
      ),
      width = 0.12,
      linewidth = 0.7,
      colour = "black"
    ) +
    geom_point(
      data = mean_results,
      aes(
        x = treatment,
        y = emmean
      ),
      shape = 18,
      size = 3.8,
      colour = "black"
    ) +
    scale_x_discrete(
      labels = treatment_labels
    ) +
    scale_colour_manual(
      values = treatment_colours
    ) +
    scale_shape_manual(
      values = c(16, 17, 15, 3)
    ) +
    expand_limits(y = 0) +
    labs(
      title = paste(
        "Total vegetation biomass:",
        location_name
      ),
      subtitle = sprintf(
        "Treatment ANOVA: F(2, %d) = %.3f, p = %.4f",
        df.residual(fit),
        a["treatment", "F value"],
        a["treatment", "Pr(>F)"]
      ),
      x = "Mowing times relative to transplanting",
      y = expression(
        "Vegetation biomass (g " * m^{-2} * ")"
      ),
      shape = "Block",
      caption = paste0(
        "Negative weeks: before transplanting; positive weeks: after transplanting.\n",
        "Coloured points: plot means of two quadrats.\n",
        "Black diamonds: adjusted means; bars: 95% confidence intervals."
      )
    ) +
    guides(
      colour = "none"
    ) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
    theme(
      legend.position = "bottom",
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0)
    )

  prefix <- tolower(
    gsub(" ", "_", location_name)
  )

  save_csv(
    anova_results,
    paste0(prefix, "_anova.csv")
  )

  save_csv(
    mean_results,
    paste0(prefix, "_adjusted_means.csv")
  )

  save_csv(
    tukey_results,
    paste0(prefix, "_tukey.csv")
  )

  ggsave(
    filename = file.path(
      output_dir,
      paste0(prefix, "_biomass.png")
    ),
    plot = figure,
    width = 7,
    height = 4.8,
    dpi = 300
  )

  ggsave(
    filename = file.path(
      output_dir,
      paste0(prefix, "_biomass.pdf")
    ),
    plot = figure,
    width = 7,
    height = 4.8
  )

  # Separate log-scale sensitivity analysis.
  # No constant is added to zero observations.
  log_anova <- NULL
  log_tukey <- NULL

  if (all(d$biomass_g_m2 > 0)) {

    log_fit <- lm(
      log(biomass_g_m2) ~ treatment + block,
      data = d,
      na.action = na.fail
    )

    log_anova <- make_anova_table(log_fit)

    log_emm <- emmeans::emmeans(
      log_fit,
      ~ treatment,
      weights = "equal"
    )

    log_tukey <- as.data.frame(
      summary(
        pairs(log_emm, adjust = "tukey"),
        infer = c(TRUE, TRUE),
        type = "link"
      )
    )

    save_csv(
      log_anova,
      paste0(prefix, "_log_anova.csv")
    )

    save_csv(
      log_tukey,
      paste0(prefix, "_log_tukey.csv")
    )
  }

  list(
    location = location_name,
    fit = fit,
    anova = anova_results,
    means = mean_results,
    tukey = tukey_results,
    figure = figure,
    log_anova = log_anova,
    log_tukey = log_tukey
  )
}

results <- setNames(
  lapply(locations, analyse_location),
  locations
)

report_location <- function(result) {

  show_table(
    result$anova,
    paste(
      result$location,
      "- ANOVA"
    )
  )

  show_table(
    result$means %>%
      select(
        treatment,
        emmean,
        SE,
        lower.CL,
        upper.CL
      ),
    paste(
      result$location,
      "- adjusted means and 95% confidence intervals"
    )
  )

  show_table(
    result$tukey %>%
      select(
        contrast,
        estimate,
        lower.CL,
        upper.CL,
        p.value
      ),
    paste(
      result$location,
      "- Tukey-adjusted pairwise comparisons"
    )
  )

  print(result$figure)

  invisible(NULL)
}
```

## Broccoli sampling location

```{r broccoli-results, results='asis'}
report_location(results[["Broccoli"]])
```

## Cover-crop sampling location

```{r cover-crop-results, results='asis'}
report_location(results[["Cover crop"]])
```

Adjusted means and pairwise differences are expressed in
grams per square metre.

Figure error bars represent individual 95% confidence intervals,
not standard errors. A negative lower confidence limit can occur
under the normal linear model and does not represent a negative
observed biomass measurement.

## Model diagnostics

Residual plots are used to assess variance patterns, normality,
and influential observations.

Shapiro-Wilk tests are supplementary. A nonsignificant normality
test does not establish that all model assumptions are satisfied.

```{r normality-tests}
normality_results <- bind_rows(
  lapply(results, function(result) {

    test <- shapiro.test(
      residuals(result$fit)
    )

    data.frame(
      Location = result$location,
      W = unname(test$statistic),
      p_value = test$p.value
    )
  })
)

knitr::kable(
  normality_results,
  digits = 4,
  caption = "Shapiro-Wilk tests of model residuals"
)

save_csv(
  normality_results,
  "residual_normality.csv"
)
```

## Log-scale sensitivity analysis

The primary analysis uses biomass in grams per square metre.
A separate natural-log analysis assesses whether conclusions
depend on the response scale.

The sensitivity analysis is not used to choose whichever model
produces a significant result. Pairwise estimates in this section
are differences in natural-log biomass.

```{r log-sensitivity-results, results='asis'}
for (location_name in locations) {

  result <- results[[location_name]]

  cat(
    "\n\n### ",
    location_name,
    "\n\n",
    sep = ""
  )

  if (is.null(result$log_anova)) {

    cat(
      "Log-scale analysis was skipped because at least one ",
      "plot mean was zero or negative.\n\n",
      sep = ""
    )

    next
  }

  show_table(
    result$log_anova,
    paste(
      location_name,
      "- log-scale ANOVA"
    )
  )

  show_table(
    result$log_tukey %>%
      select(
        contrast,
        estimate,
        lower.CL,
        upper.CL,
        p.value
      ),
    paste(
      location_name,
      "- Tukey comparisons on the natural-log scale"
    )
  )
}
```

## Interpretation

Treatment differences are interpreted separately for the two
sampling locations because their sampling protocols differ.

The treatment comparison concerns three mowing schedules:

- T2: one mowing event before transplanting and two after transplanting.
- T3: one mowing event before transplanting and one after transplanting.
- T4: one mowing event before transplanting only.

A nonsignificant result indicates insufficient evidence of a
treatment difference under the fitted model. It does not demonstrate
that treatments are equivalent.

Conclusions should consider estimated differences, confidence
intervals, residual diagnostics, and sensitivity to response scale.

Because all recorded species are included, these results concern
total vegetation biomass. They do not independently establish
effects on weed-only biomass or broccoli yield.
